title: Localize TutorPinValidationError.message instead of leaking raw English into tutor PIN screens

evidence.quote:
return const TutorPinValidationError(
        message: 'Tutor PIN must be exactly 4 numeric digits.',

why: TutorPinValidationError carries a hand-written English message that both tutor_pin_setup_screen.dart and tutor_pin_entry_gate.dart assign straight into _errorMessage with no AppLocalizations resolution. The on-screen numpad only ever calls verifyTutorPin/setTutorPin with exactly 4 digits, so this specific branch is currently unreachable via the shipped UI — but it is a live landmine: any future caller (automation, a text-entry fallback, a reused validator) will render untranslated English to Hebrew users. This is the exact pattern already fixed for TutorGrantFailure elsewhere in the same feature, so the fix here is a straightforward extension of an established precedent.
recommendation: Replace the message field with a stable code/enum and resolve it via AppLocalizations in both screens, mirroring the TutorGrantFailure fix.
acceptance_criteria: TutorPinValidationError carries a code, not a literal English string
tutor_pin_setup_screen.dart and tutor_pin_entry_gate.dart resolve the code via AppLocalizations with EN+HE parity
a widget test forces the validation-error branch (e.g. directly invoking the service with a malformed pin) and asserts the localized string renders
